equity.level_reason: Age-adjusted firearm homicide rates are reported for each race and Hispanic-origin group within sex, and the highest and lowest groups are described, but no difference or ratio is computed and nothing is framed as a disparity, so the level is capped at 2.

ev.q: Age-Adjusted Rates* of Firearm-Related Homicide, † by Race, § Hispanic Origin, and Sex
Black or African American (Black) males had the highest age-adjusted rate of firearm-related homicide (52.9 deaths per 100,000 standard population), and Asian males had the lowest rate (1.5).
Males had higher rates than females across all race and Hispanic origin groups.
Deaths per 100,000 population are age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population

equity.equity_measurement: Race groups are non-Hispanic with Hispanic origin as a separate group; NH/OPI not shown because of small numbers; death-certificate misclassification may bias Asian, AI/AN and Hispanic rates.

notes: The structural record is sound; age standardization plus race-within-sex rates support stratified/adjusted depth, and values are only set side by side (scale null).
